overpass_alps.json in this folder is data of OpenStreetMap,
https://www.openstreetmap.org, © OpenStreetMap contributors, available under
the Open Database License, https://opendatacommons.org/licenses/odbl/1-0/.
It is not covered by the licence of the code around it.

It was recorded on 2026-11-19 at 18:09 UTC from the Overpass instance
"Overpass Europe" at https://ovp.dresel.systems/api/interpreter, which
holds Geofabrik's extract of Europe and said that its copy of OpenStreetMap
was of 2026-11-18 21:21:02 UTC. The main public instance, overpass-api.de,
and overpass.private.coffee did not accept connections from the machine
that recorded it. The query was the adapter's own for the box of the first
region, with a time limit of 60 seconds where the adapter asks for 90. The
instance took 53 seconds:

    [out:json][timeout:60][bbox:46.3,9.4,48.5,17.2];
    (nwr["sport"~"free_flying"];nwr["free_flying:site"];
     nwr["free_flying:takeoff"];nwr["free_flying:landing"];
     nwr["free_flying:towing"];nwr["free_flying:training"];);
    out tags center qt;

All 517 elements of the answer are in the file, in the order of the
answer, each with its type, number and position as the instance sent them.
One thing was changed: of an element's tags only those the adapter reads
are kept (name, ele, sport, direction, the free_flying:* keys for uses,
orientation, official, paragliding, hanggliding, unsafe, school, shop,
repair, club and tandem, and shop, office, amenity, tourism, craft and
building). 89 other keys were removed, among them operator, phone, email
and website: an operator is often a person, and this repository holds no
personal data. The file is written with one element per line, which the
instance does not do.

To record it again: send the query above to an Overpass instance, keep the
tags listed, then run the tests with VENTI_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 and review what
changed. The test "the_first_region_holds_what_was_measured" pins the
counts that docs/data-sources.md quotes.

overpass_damaged.json is not OpenStreetMap's data as published: it is
eleven elements of overpass_alps.json, ten of them deliberately broken or
changed, to test how the adapter reports what it cannot read and what it
leaves out. The test that uses it says how each is broken.
overpass_timeout.json is what an instance answers when it runs out of
time: written from the Overpass API's documented behaviour, not recorded.
To verify against a real answer of that kind.

Sites in OpenStreetMap are entered by anyone. A record is no permission
to fly and no statement that a place is safe.
